paragraphs: You can say and think whatever you like, but I know exactly how you feel. You've had it the fuck up to here with vibe-coding, some of you with life itself. Your jaw clenches with anger, then comes the fatigue you want to hide in emptiness. Let the emptiness fill the whole world. Better that than this continuous suffering.
And all of it is because of piss-soaked Anthropic. It plays with your nerves, and it's progressing in this game. Beating you by an ever bigger score.
I don't know how else to describe the releases with which this manufacturer of dick cheese has been indulging us in this already difficult year.

Right now I've dropped everything and have spent the whole day guessing whether the task will switch to Opus; I'll be sitting in one session holding the Ultracode safety catch down against the kickback, not exhaling and losing time and limits on all the other subscriptions, since you can't touch the mouse.

Throwing an entire prompt pack that's been in the making for four hours into the trash and reverting all changes, because it turned out Fable thought brilliantly but for some reason ignored one parameter in the repo without which all the prompts are at minimum a blocker for Codex, at maximum the destruction of everything that worked fine (good thing I noticed in time).
And at the end of such a day you sit and think, in what way is this fucking better than sewing panama hats in Bali.
Stability of operation is, after all, a far more important parameter in the quality formula than peak reasoning.
Doesn't mean peak reasoning isn't needed, just not at the cost of stability.
Two options here:
Either Anthropic fixes this, looking at the churn.
Or I'm not understanding something and never will, due to too limited a number of brain folds.

But what will definitely happen — the market will howl and mutter about how Anthropic fucked everyone, even if they never press another button, since the info in the infosphere these days is 99% from those whose OpenClaw on a Mac mini automated their whole business by itself, and there's nothing to be done about that anymore.
Some didn't understand about the mouse, so I'll explain, only first please take a good thorough dump, I warned you.
If you want Ultracode to work longer than 0 minutes, you have to simply hold it down with the mouse, and then it doesn't switch it off.

Don't ask how I found out. I've simply tried every fucking thing. Nothing helped with the nerves, don't bother looking. You'll hate these motherfuckers, whatever cheat codes you enter — doesn't fucking matter at all. Nothing will help. Only darkness ahead:**
You have to really, really love… I don't even know what. Dick? Sucking?
…to use Fable 5's services without a subscription, for API tokens exchanged for dollars:)))

The other day I upgraded my hand-written Telegram bridge; it can now do a lot of pleasant things I need, like monitoring progress across active Claude App sessions with a pulse into Telegram, and much more.
And for some reason the model also added data on how much my request would have cost via API, even though I of course make these requests through the subscription.
Two letters, AV, sent by accident would have cost me 11 dollars and 85 cents. And not Kazakhstani dollars, but fucking American ones.
That's what the dekulakization of the future looks like :D

Here we supposedly have a channel about vibe-wanking, yet the sneaky hobbits didn't even tell their brothers and sisters of the ring that the GitHub connector to GPT PRO has long since started working in the web version, and you can get Fable+ reasoning about a repo or even a group of repos directly from GPT PRO itself.
Given what I needed Fable for, I no longer fucking need it now))))))))))

GPT PRO just solved three colossal dilemmas for me that I've been fucking around with for two weeks. One of them, by the way, even Fable didn't solve. It's a dilemma about the site's interface. Fable did decently, better than 5.5 in Codex, but what GPT 5.5 PRO just handed me is simply a fucking cannon.
And GPT 5.5 PRO didn't produce it itself; it simply wrote a prompt for Claude Design that took the result to some completely stratospheric level.

Turns out that all these two weeks I was tormenting Claude Design with the right words, and conceptually more or less correctly too, but I hadn't set one single invariant, because of which it kept producing something quite other than what I needed. GPT 5.5 PRO caught that from my prompt full of fucking agonies. Fable / Opus 4.8 / GPT 5.5 xhigh in Codex — didn't catch it.
In short, GPT 5.5 PRO IS GREAT for vibe-wanking AGAIN
In the latest Codex update they visualized task progress very nicely =)
Didn't think I needed this until I saw how it works. I think this is exactly the emotion users of products should feel when the products invent the right little piece of UI/UX =)

Fuck, folks, how the fuck does it happen that every day, drowning in dense vibe-wanking, I learn a TON of skills, and they only thicken in front of me? Are you engineers completely fucking nuts to have invented so many different things?!?!??!?! =)))))

Well, first of all, my respect, of course. I don't understand how projects even came into being with such a quantity of assorted shit that has to be accounted for/studied/applied/refactored just to knock together an MVP, never mind solid scalable products.
Second, may all of it rest in peace, of course. I'm telling you straight: within a short time all this crap will be canceled.

I think when the LLM reaches a certain level of self-sufficiency, it'll invent its own language and replace the Internet with itself, and no multi-story routing of every kind of shit will need to be done.

Honestly, it seems to me such a dominance of every kind of moronic technical shit was never needed. The Internet and IT live not thanks to it but in spite of it. I'm sure this zoo is nothing but the Lord's sins. Greed: when a framework or a language or an entire platform was created with the barrier purpose of keeping outside players out. Pride: when one team or even one person who'd gained influence in the market managed to create a little sect and impose on them his sense of beauty, in fact sucked out of a finger hard to distinguish by appearance from a dick.
And murder: you want those guys over there to die so badly that we'd rather code in a made-up language, just so not one extra dollar sticks to those freaks' pockets.
Etc.

Somewhere in there flickered the blue sin of true gayness, and the sin of fucking coder faggotry, and around a hard but suspiciously soft and warm phallic symbol the guild of stretched-out sweaters raced around on rear-wheel drive, fucking not in a BMW.
I'm tired of learning all of this, of course.
Good thing GPT 5.6 is already coming on Tuesday. At least that's what reached me from buddies at OpenAI. Unless something fucks up, that is; it's already supposed to have come out a couple of times.

Closed my eyes, sweetly hung in the blissful weightlessness of a body heading straight into deep sleep, and suddenly a thought smacked me across the fucking face: so vibe-wankers are, it turns out, those very “computer guys”:))))

That's exactly what they used to call those dorky-looking types who'd take on any computer work and do it as shittily as possible, then, with a sense of over-fulfilled duty, go collect rejections from the Tolkien girls)

By the way, I also think it might make sense to slap together a digest on the release of all significant models and their new properties, so as not to wait for someone to talk about them in the discussion group and not waste precious time searching for this info. I never search, by the way, because it takes a fuckton of time you'd need to have. And when would you vibe-wank? And when would you run the business? And when would you give the tenderest one a kiss of love? And when would you watch shows? And when would you drink beer?

Or do you think that would be fucking spam, and you don't fucking need info about all the new models released in the last X days and their wonderful properties? After all, it's still somehow expensive to run top models locally purely on hardware, and in the cloud it's already known which models to use and how much they cost?:)
If it would be useful to read here after all, then how often? Once a minute? An hour? A day? A week?
